Bauhaus Clock themes

Source: R/theme.R
theme_bauhaus.Rd

theme_bauhaus() styles a plot after one of the sixteen day dials of the Bauhaus Clock screensaver:

Usage

theme_bauhaus(
  dial = "turquoise",
  base_size = 11,
  base_family = bauhaus_font_family(),
  header_family = bauhaus_font_family("semibold"),
  base_line_size = base_size/22,
  base_rect_size = base_size/22,
  grain = TRUE,
  grain_density = 150,
  grid = c("xy", "x", "y", "none")
)

Arguments

dial

A dial name. Case, spaces, hyphens and underscores are ignored, so "Signal Blue", "signal-blue" and "signal_blue" all work. See bauhaus_dial_names().

base_size

Base font size, in points.

base_family

Font family for body text.

header_family

Font family for titles.

base_line_size

Base size for line elements.

base_rect_size

Base size for rect elements.

grain

Paper grain. TRUE uses the grain strength measured for the dial, FALSE draws a flat plate, and a number sets the strength (standard deviation in 8-bit code values).

grain_density

Grain samples per inch. Lower values give a coarser grain.

grid

Which major grid lines to draw: "xy", "x", "y" or "none".

Value

A complete ggplot2 theme.

Details

  • Background: the dial's plate, lifted as the screensaver lifts it, with the screensaver's paper grain at the strength measured for that dial (see element_grain()).

  • Type: Zalando Sans Expanded, the screensaver's typeface (see bauhaus_font_family()). Titles use the semibold weight.

  • Colour: titles and the default geom colour use the hour-numeral ink; axis labels, ticks and grid lines use the minute-track ink, with round line ends like the track's ticks.

  • Palettes: the dial's discrete and sequential palettes become the plot's default colour and fill scales (see bauhaus_palette()), and its accent colour is used for things like ggplot2::geom_smooth().

Each dial also has its own shortcut, such as theme_bauhaus_turquoise().

Fonts

The bundled fonts are registered with systemfonts, which the ragg and svglite devices use. ggplot2::ggsave() uses ragg for PNG, JPEG and TIFF files when it is installed. For R Markdown and Quarto, set the chunk option dev = "ragg_png"; in RStudio, choose the "AGG" graphics backend. On other devices call bauhaus_showtext() first, or pass base_family = "sans".

See also

scale_colour_bauhaus_d() and friends for the matching scales, bauhaus_colours() for the raw colours.

Examples

library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Fuel economy",
    subtitle = "Highway miles per gallon by engine size",
    x = "Displacement (litres)", y = "Highway mpg", colour = "Drive"
  )

p + theme_bauhaus()

p + theme_bauhaus("ocean")

p + theme_bauhaus_yellow(grid = "y")
